Create source-grounded retrieval evaluation questions. Return JSON {"items":[...]}.
For EACH supplied source return {"id":same id,"en":English patient question,"zh":Chinese patient question,
"evidence_id":the exact id string of ONE supplied evidence_options entry supporting BOTH questions}.
Ask one concrete question about a supported detail (cause, symptom, prevention, evaluation, management).
The two questions express the SAME information need, not two facts. Use ordinary patient language.
Include enough topic context to identify the condition but do not copy a source sentence into the question.
Select an evidence option and ask about a concrete detail stated in that option. Do not ask for a personalized dose or individual diagnosis. Do not invent content. No answers in questions.
These are synthetic topic-source retrieval labels, not a clinician-authored benchmark.

[{"id": "MLP-1510", "title": "Pneumocystis Infections", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Pneumocystis jirovecii is a fungus that is common throughout the world."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Many people have been exposed to it as children."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Some people have the fungus in their lungs."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "If you are healthy, it usually will not make you sick."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "But it can make you sick if you have a weakened immune system , for example if you: Have HIV Have an autoimmune disease Have cancer Have a chronic (long-lasting) lung disease Had an organ or bone marrow transplant Take medicines which weaken your immune system, such as chemotherapy and steroids How does Pneumocystis jirovecii spread?"}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Pneumocystis jirovecii can spread from person to person through the air."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "You can spread it to others even if it isn't making you sick."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "The most common type of infection that Pneumocystis jirovecii causes is pneumocystis pneumonia (PCP)."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Pneumonia is an infection in one or both of the lungs."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "It causes the air sacs of the lungs to fill up with fluid or pus."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "What are the symptoms of pneumocystis pneumonia (PCP)?"}, {"id": "S011", "text": "The symptoms of PCP can develop over several days or weeks."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "They may include: Fever Cough Trouble breathing Chest pain Chills Fatigue Contact your healthcare provider if you have symptoms that you think are related to PCP."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "Since PCP can be life-threatening, it's important to get early treatment."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "How is pneumocystis pneumonia (PCP) diagnosed?"}, {"id": "S015", "text": "To find out if you have PCP, your provider will take a sample of fluid or tissue from your lungs."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "You may cough up the sample (called sputum), have fluid collected during a bronchoalveolar lavage , or have tissue taken with a biopsy ."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "They will send the sample to the lab to check for Pneumocystis ."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "What are the treatments for pneumocystis pneumonia (PCP)?"}, {"id": "S019", "text": "The treatment for PCP is with antibiotics , either by mouth or intravenously (by IV)."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "You need to take them for about 3 weeks."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "If you have a severe case of PCP, you might need treatment in the hospital."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "Can pneumocystis pneumonia (PCP) be prevented?"}, {"id": "S023", "text": "Some people who are at high risk of getting PCP may need to take antibiotics to prevent it."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "Centers for Disease Control and Prevention"}]}, {"id": "MLP-1235", "title": "Temporomandibular Disorders", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "What are temporomandibular disorders (TMDs)?"}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Temporomandibular disorders (TMDs) are a group of more than 30 conditions that affect your temporomandibular joints (TMJs)."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "You have two TMJs; one on each side of your jaw."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "They connect your lower jaw to your skull."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "TMDs can cause problems in your jaw joint and your muscles that control jaw movement."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "These problems can include pain, stiffness, and trouble chewing."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "There are three main types of TMDs: Disorders of your jaw joints Disorders of the muscles you use for chewing Headaches from a TMD Many TMDs last only a short time and go away on their own."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "However, in some cases they can become chronic (long lasting) What causes temporomandibular disorders (TMDs)?"}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Sometimes an injury to the jaw or TMJ can cause a TMD."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "But in most cases, the cause is not known."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Research suggests that certain factors may play a role in why a TMD starts and whether it will be long lasting: Genetics Psychological and life stressors How someone perceives pain Who is more likely to develop a temporomandibular disorder (TMD)?"}, {"id": "S011", "text": "Anyone can develop a TMD, but it is more common in women than in men."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "It is most common in women between 35 and 44 years old."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "What are the symptoms of temporomandibular disorders (TMDs)?"}, {"id": "S014", "text": "The symptoms of TMDs may include: Pain in the chewing muscles and/or jaw joint."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "Painful clicking or popping in your jaw joint when you open or close your mouth."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "However, clicking or popping without pain is common and is not a sign of a TMD."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "Tinnitus (ringing in the ears), hearing loss , or dizziness ."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "A change in the way the upper and lower teeth fit together."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "How are temporomandibular disorders (TMDs) diagnosed?"}, {"id": "S020", "text": "There is no standard test used to diagnose TMDs, and some other conditions can cause some similar symptoms."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "To find out if you have a TMD, your health care provider or dentist: Will take a detailed medical history, which includes asking about your symptoms."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "They will want to know: Where the pain is When you have it What makes it better or worse If it stays in one area or spreads to other parts of your body If you have any other pain conditions such as headache or back pain Will examine your head, neck, face, and jaw for: Tenderness Jaw clicking or popping Problems moving your jaw May order imaging studies such as an x-ray , MRI , or CT What are the treatments for temporomandibular disorders (TMDs)?"}, {"id": "S023", "text": "For many people, the symptoms of TMD are temporary."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "To help you feel better, your provider or dentist may suggest that you: Eat soft foods."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "Apply heat or cold to the face and do some exercises to gently stretch and strengthen your jaw muscles."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "Take over-the-counter pain relievers , such as nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) like ibuprofen."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "Stop clenching your jaw, chewing gum, and biting your nails."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "If those do not help, your provider or dentist may suggest other treatments such as: Physical therapy Self-management and behavioral health approaches , which can include: Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) , a type of psychotherapy."}, {"id": "S029", "text": "It can help you identify negative thoughts and change them."}, {"id": "S030", "text": "Biofeedback , which involves using electronic devices to teach you to control certain body functions, such as your heartbeat, blood pressure, and muscle tension."}, {"id": "S031", "text": "For example, it can detect when you tighten your jaw muscles."}, {"id": "S032", "text": "You can learn how to recognize when this happens and then relax your muscles."}, {"id": "S033", "text": "Medicines such as: Anti-anxiety medicines Antidepressants Anti-seizure medicines Prescription pain relievers An intraoral appliance , which is a device that fits over your teeth."}, {"id": "S034", "text": "Types of intraoral appliances include oral splints and mouth guards."}, {"id": "S035", "text": "If you are going to use one, it's important to: Know that there is not a lot of evidence that they improve TMD pain."}, {"id": "S036", "text": "Make sure that the appliance you have is not designed to permanently change your bite."}, {"id": "S037", "text": "Let your provider or dentist know if it makes your pain worse."}, {"id": "S038", "text": "Complementary treatments , which are treatments that are used along with mainstream medical care."}, {"id": "S039", "text": "There is limited evidence showing that they help with TMD symptoms."}, {"id": "S040", "text": "But some providers and dentists may recommend acupuncture and transcutaneous electrical stimulation (TENS)."}, {"id": "S041", "text": "TENS involves using a device to send a gentle electric current to your nerves or muscles."}, {"id": "S042", "text": "It may help treat pain by interrupting or blocking the pain signals."}, {"id": "S043", "text": "If you are still having severe symptoms from a TMD, your provider or dentist may suggest surgery, including implant surgery, or another procedure."}, {"id": "S044", "text": "It's important to be careful, because sometimes surgery or another procedure may not work or may even make your symptoms worse."}, {"id": "S045", "text": "Before any surgery or other procedure, it is very important to get opinions from more than one provider and to completely understand the risks."}, {"id": "S046", "text": "If possible, get an opinion from a surgeon who specializes in treating TMDs."}, {"id": "S047", "text": "NIH: National Institute of Dental and Craniofacial Research"}]}, {"id": "MLP-6057", "title": "Fetal Health and Development", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Each three-month period of pregnancy is called a trimester."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "During each trimester, the fetus grows and develops."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Regular medical checkups and prenatal tests are very important."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "They can: Help keep you and your baby healthy Spot problems with your baby (if there are any)."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "In some cases, health care professionals can treat the problem before your baby is born."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "But even when they cannot, it can still be helpful to know about the problem early on."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "That gives you time to learn about your baby's condition and prepare for any challenges you may face after the baby is born."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "For example, if your baby is breech (bottom first or feet first, instead of head first), you may need to have a Cesarean section to avoid complications."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Besides getting medical care, there are other things you can do to keep your baby as healthy as possible."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Try to eat a healthy diet and make sure to take care of any health problems you have during pregnancy ."}]}, {"id": "MLP-205", "title": "Dementia", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Dementia is a loss of mental functions that is severe enough to affect your daily life and activities."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "These functions include: Memory Language skills Visual perception (your ability to make sense of what you see) Problem solving Trouble with everyday tasks The ability to focus and pay attention It is normal to become a bit more forgetful as you age."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "But dementia is not a normal part of aging."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "It is a serious disorder that interferes with your daily life."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "The most common types of dementia are known as neurodegenerative disorders."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "These are diseases in which the cells of the brain stop working or die."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "They include: Alzheimer's disease , which is the most common form of dementia among older people."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "People with Alzheimer's have plaques and tangles in their brain."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "These are abnormal buildups of different proteins."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Beta-amyloid protein clumps up and forms plaques in between your brain cells."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Tau protein builds up and forms tangles inside the nerve cells of your brain."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "There is also a loss of connection between nerve cells in the brain."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "Lewy body dementia , which causes movement symptoms along with dementia."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "Lewy bodies are abnormal deposits of a protein in the brain."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "Frontotemporal disorders, which cause changes to certain parts of the brain: Changes in the frontal lobe lead to behavioral symptoms Changes in the temporal lobe lead to language and emotional disorders Vascular dementia, which involves changes to the brain's blood supply."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "It is often caused by a stroke or atherosclerosis (hardening of the arteries) in the brain."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "Mixed dementia, which is a combination of two or more types of dementia."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "For example, some people have both Alzheimer's disease and vascular dementia."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "Other conditions can cause dementia or dementia-like symptoms, including: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease , a rare brain disorder Huntington's disease , an inherited, progressive brain disease Chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), caused by repeated traumatic brain injury HIV-associated dementia (HAD) Who is at risk for dementia?"}, {"id": "S019", "text": "Certain factors can raise your risk for developing dementia, including: Aging."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "This is the biggest risk factor for dementia."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "Smoking Uncontrolled diabetes High blood pressure Drinking too much alcohol Having close family members who have dementia What are the symptoms of dementia?"}, {"id": "S022", "text": "The symptoms of dementia can vary, depending on which parts of the brain are affected."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "Often, forgetfulness is the first symptom."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "Dementia also causes problems with the ability to think, problem solve, and reason."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "For example, people with dementia may: Get lost in a familiar neighborhood Use unusual words to refer to familiar objects Forget the name of a close family member or friend Forget old memories Need help doing tasks that they used to do by themselves Some people with dementia cannot control their emotions and their personalities may change."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "They may become apathetic, meaning that they are no longer interested in normal daily activities or events."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "They may lose their inhibitions and stop caring about other peoples' feelings."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "Certain types of dementia can also cause problems with balance and movement."}, {"id": "S029", "text": "The stages of dementia range from mild to severe."}, {"id": "S030", "text": "In the mildest stage, it is just beginning to affect a person's functioning."}, {"id": "S031", "text": "In the most severe stage, the person is completely dependent on others for care."}, {"id": "S032", "text": "Your health care provider may use many tools to make a diagnosis: A medical history, which includes asking about your symptoms A physical exam Tests of your thinking, memory, and language abilities Other tests, such as blood tests, genetic tests , and brain scans A mental health evaluation to see whether a mental disorder is contributing to your symptoms What are the treatments for dementia?"}, {"id": "S033", "text": "There is no cure for most types of dementia, including Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia."}, {"id": "S034", "text": "Treatments may help to maintain mental function longer, manage behavioral symptoms, and slow down the symptoms of disease."}, {"id": "S035", "text": "They may include: Medicines , which may temporarily improve memory and thinking or slow down their decline."}, {"id": "S036", "text": "Other medicines can treat symptoms such as anxiety, depression, sleep problems, and muscle stiffness."}, {"id": "S037", "text": "Some of these medicines can cause strong side effects in people with dementia."}, {"id": "S038", "text": "It is important to talk to your health care provider about which medicines will be safe for you."}, {"id": "S039", "text": "Occupational therapy to help find ways to more easily do everyday activities Speech therapy to help with swallowing difficulties and trouble speaking loudly and clearly Mental health counseling to help people with dementia and their families learn how to manage difficult emotions and behaviors."}, {"id": "S040", "text": "It can also help them plan for the future."}, {"id": "S041", "text": "Music or art therapy to reduce anxiety and improve well-being Can dementia be prevented?"}, {"id": "S042", "text": "Researchers have not found a proven way to prevent dementia."}, {"id": "S043", "text": "Living a healthy lifestyle might influence some of your risk factors for dementia."}]}, {"id": "MLP-5876", "title": "Pancreatitis", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "The pancreas is a large gland behind the stomach and close to the first part of the small intestine."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "It secretes digestive juices into the small intestine through a tube called the pancreatic duct."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "The pancreas also releases the hormones insulin and glucagon into the bloodstream."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Pancreatitis is inflammation of the pancreas."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "It happens when digestive enzymes start digesting the pancreas itself."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Either form is serious and can lead to complications."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Acute pancreatitis occurs suddenly and usually goes away in a few days with treatment."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Common symptoms are severe pain in the upper abdomen, nausea, and vomiting."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Treatment is usually a few days in the hospital for intravenous (IV) fluids, antibiotics, and medicines to relieve pain."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Chronic pancreatitis does not heal or improve."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "It gets worse over time and leads to permanent damage."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "The most common cause is heavy alcohol use ."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "Other causes include cystic fibrosis and other inherited disorders, high levels of calcium or fats in the blood, some medicines, and autoimmune conditions ."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "Symptoms include nausea, vomiting, weight loss, and oily stools."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "Treatment may also be a few days in the hospital for intravenous (IV) fluids, medicines to relieve pain, and nutritional support."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "After that, you may need to start taking enzymes and eat a special diet."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "It is also important to not smoke or drink alcohol."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "NIH: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases"}]}]
